title: Why Yawns Are Contagious (Probably)
description:
You just yawned reading that, didn't you? Here's what scientists actually think is going on when yawns spread between people.

Educational content, not medical advice.

#shorts #wellbeing #psychologyfacts

scenes.text: Just reading the word yawn makes a lot of people yawn. That's not a coincidence.
Contagious yawning shows up in humans as early as childhood, and researchers have also seen it in chimps and dogs.
One leading theory ties it to empathy. Studies have found people yawn more in response to those they feel socially close to.
Brain imaging studies point to regions involved in social awareness lighting up during contagious yawning.
It's still an active area of research, and not every scientist agrees on exactly why it happens.
But the pattern itself is well documented: yawns spread through a room like a quiet, involuntary form of social mirroring.
